title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Several Provisions on Audio and Video Recordings of Court Proceedings
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the "Several Provisions on Audio and Video Recording of Trial Activities"

Fa Fa [2010] No. 33

All local people's courts at various levels across the country, all military courts, all railway transport intermediate courts and basic courts, all maritime courts, and all courts of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

The Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on Audio and Video Recording of Trial Activities" are hereby issued to you for earnest implementation.

August 16, 2010

Several Provisions on Audio and Video Recording of Trial Activities

To strengthen trial management, improve the method of court record-keeping, protect the litigation rights of the parties, and promote judicial fairness, in accordance with relevant procedural laws and in light of the actual work of the people's courts, the following provisions are hereby made on audio and video recording of trial activities:

1. When a people's court opens a court session to hear a criminal, civil, or administrative case under the first-instance ordinary procedure or the second-instance procedure, it shall conduct simultaneous audio or video recording of the entire trial activity. For cases under summary procedure and other procedures, audio or video recording of the trial activity shall be conducted as necessary.

For trial activities conducted outside a trial courtroom, such as circuit trials, if conditions for audio or video recording are not available, such recording may be omitted.

2. A people's court shall install audio recording equipment in its trial courtrooms; where conditions permit, video recording equipment shall also be installed. A people's tribunal may install audio or video recording equipment in some of its trial courtrooms based on actual needs.

3. Audio and video recording of a trial shall commence from the start of the court session by the court clerk or other staff member, and the litigation participants shall be informed thereof, and shall end upon the closure of the court session. Except for recesses and mediation activities that are not suitable for audio or video recording, the audio and video recording shall not be interrupted.

The court clerk shall record in the court record the start and end times of the audio and video recording and whether any interruption occurred.

4. If a party or other litigation participant raises an objection to the court record and applies for correction, the court clerk shall play back the audio and video recording for verification and correction. If the correction is not made, the application shall be recorded in the case file.

5. A people's court shall use specialized equipment to store the audio and video recording of the trial and shall preserve it as case material in the case file by means of CDs or other media. Where conditions exist for the parties, defenders, agents ad litem, and others to review it at the people's court, it shall be placed in the principal case file. Without the permission of the people's court, no person may duplicate, photograph, record, or disseminate the audio and video recording of the trial.

The retention period for the audio and video recording of the trial shall be the same as the retention period for the case file.

6. A people's court shall take measures such as superimposing synchronized recording time or other measures to ensure the authenticity and integrity of the audio and video recording of the trial. Any person who damages the audio and video recording of the trial or tampers with its content shall be subject to corresponding administrative or legal liability.

If the audio and video recording content is incomplete or non-existent due to equipment or technical reasons, the person responsible for the recording shall make a written explanation, which shall be attached to the file after being reviewed and signed by the presiding judge or the chief judge of the division. An incomplete audio and video recording of the trial shall still be stored and included in the file.

7. During the trial, if a litigation participant or observer violates courtroom discipline or relevant legal provisions, disrupts courtroom order, or hinders the smooth progress of the litigation, the audio and video recording of the trial may be used as evidence to pursue their legal liability.

8. If a party or other litigation participant considers that the trial activity was不规范 (not standardized) or involved illegal conduct, the people's court shall conduct an investigation and verification by reviewing the audio and video recording of the trial.

9. The president of the people's court, the chief judge of a division, or the disciplinary inspection and supervision department may access the audio and video recording of the trial as required by work needs. Access to audio and video recordings of cases tried in closed sessions shall comply with relevant confidentiality provisions.

10. Higher people's courts may, based on local circumstances, formulate detailed implementation rules for these provisions regarding the technology, management, and application of audio and video recording of trials.

11. Where a people's court conducts other activities such as trials, enforcement, hearings, or接待来访 (meetings with visitors), and requires audio or video recording, these provisions shall be applied mutatis mutandis.
